test_title: PYST 57: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Reasoning (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: reasoning
question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 268 667 457 856 426 (Right)

(Example: 697 - First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7) (NOTE: All operations to be done from left to right.)

If 1 is subtracted from the first digit of every number, in how many numbers will the third digit be exactly divisible by the first digit?
solution: Given: (Left) 268 667 457 856 426 (Right) If 1 is subtracted from the first digit of every number, we get 268 → first digit becomes 2 − 1 = 1; third digit = 8 → 8 ÷ 1 = 8 (divisible) 667 → first digit becomes 6 − 1 = 5; third digit = 7 → 7 ÷ 5 (not divisible)
